data: Great game 10/10 definitely worth a play through if you like story driven games
Games really good looking, music is amazing, gameplay is really fun and the story (so far) is great, characters are interesting and the world,
Amazing graphics, intriguing storyline, great characters, a lot of replayability 10/10 would recommend
10/10 the story is peak, the characters are peak, and the dlc are all peak
Great game the story is 10/10, a lot of content
combat system - not fun, really clunky and full of bugs, one of the worst ive ever seen
Can't recommend until they fix all the issues with their blighted EA app
It was boring, repetitive and I saw no point in slogging through hours of the same
i think people are a tad bit dramatic about this game. it's fun, but i can concede it is pretty bloated with optional content that doesn't serve the narrative.
Baught this game on ps3,ps4,origin and finally steam..atleast 200 hrs between all platforms..good enough to come back to 6 years later..def a fantasy rpg for the collection

90 % of the game is boring, 10 % is perfect. It is worthy to play the game because of those 10 %.

MILD SPOILERS AHEAD

Perfect:

- your own beautiful castle (hub) with many people in and a lot to do
- feeling that your actually leading the inquisition and helping the continent
- mission Wicked Eyes and Wicked Hearts - where you are searching for an unknown assassin on a royal ball (I have never ever played better and more thrilling quest in any other RPG)
- companions and their personalities, talks and quests (my favorite: Sera, Solas)

Good:

- dragon fights
- fade missions
- lore of the world

Boring and bad:

- boring generic quests (including main story missions), boring generic maps, and a lot of filler (this is 90 % of the Game!!!!!)
- average combat
- solving a chain side quest leading to a big secret and/or treasure - you get a generic reward /or stupid and boring ending (...like all quests of this type will let you down miserably...)
- boring and generic ending (not including dlc)

Characters are well contoured, the side quests help explore the world, but don't detract from the min story, and the team roster allows one to change the play style with ease depending on mood. Really enjoyable game even in 2024, especially if taking it lightly.

Honestly, after playing Veilguard this shit is GOATed. I can't wait to go back, slap on some mods, and kiss Cullen. Veilguard was so disappointing that it makes me truly appreciate the other games that came before it.

It has a wonderful plot and a structured base for continuing the plots of DAO, DA2. Especially being able to explore a bunch of new romantic content. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves this type of gaming content. Also Commander Cullen will forever be in my dreams as the cute and handsomest man ever.

Classic game, quality IP from Bioware. If you haven't played other entries in the series, you will still enjoy this game, and it won't be confusing nor feel like you've "missed out" on parts of the story.

Also, this may be controversial, but the voice actor for Varric is NOT the same voice actor as Garrus.
Aside from a few minor bugs this game is very well made if you enjoy fantasy high adventure and don't mind the grind of fetch quests. Every quest is worth doing for the best end result though.

DO NOT buy on PC, relies on EA app that is terminally broken. Tons of customer complaints that EA app doesn't load the game, since early 2023, and NO solution given. "Its on our end" the EA support tech said.
They're not going to fix it.
Get it on Console so you don't have to use the EA app.

Game is pretty cool. Forced EA launcher and account sucks. Having to play online sucks. Also profanity and street language is out of place in a fantasy game and is immersion breaking, why do game devs feel the need to lace everything with foul language to make people think it's "cool"? I'm also tired of having gay this and gay that shoved in my face all the time. Dragon Age Origins is a much better game.

The fact that it requires an active Origin connection (and that Origin has such frequent connection problems) is a serious downside to TRYING TO play this game.

That said, if Origin does manage to start correctly -- you will likely have to reboot TWICE each time you want to play DA:I, because "End Task" will not kill Origin processes all the way -- then it can be a pretty fun game. ;-)

i want to throw a slice of cheese on solas' head to see if it sticks

UPDATE: i've had various copies of this game for over a decade but only now have i properly gotten the hang of it (and gotten the hell out of the hinterlands) and the more time goes on the more i'm glad that i didn't figure this game out as an obnoxious blorbo-hungry teenager, because if i'd gotten my mitts on cullen rutherford back then, it would have permanently changed my brain chemistry. hell, i think he's permanently changed my brain chemistry now.

One of the greatest frabchises ever made. Great game great story great characters and you can play with different classes and races. If you want to understand the world better it's reccomended to play the previous games (Dragon Age (Dragon Age Origins and Dragon Age 2). Reccomended if you like the genre.

I played Dragon Age Origins before and I love it very much so I picked this game - GOTY edition - up.
The first time I played this for good few hours, I felt like, "Oh.. why is it like this? why did it win GOTY award." I stopped playing it.

Years has passed and I decided to give this game a try. Maybe I played this with a new perspective, I have let go the mechanic of Dragon Age Origins or I have accepted that things change, new way of gaming is changing lol. I finished the game. I beat the final boss and could say this game is good, despite it crashed a lot of times (maybe more than 50 times) during my play.

Give it a try if you are on the border of playing it. Give it a try for sure if you like action RPG.
While some characters can come off as lacking and the writing can be a bit stale I still find it to be a fun dragon age game to sink your time in.

This game is excellent and all for the console.
Here on PC, it can become a nightmare ONLY because of the (EA APP)

Played this game for almost 160 hours and wanted to play the game today again, but the EA APP launcher is stuck and reopens itself over and over again when trying to open the game. No files have been changed, no updates, no removing or relocating of any files since last playing the game.

Tried updating Windows, GeForce, and Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. Nothing of that worked... uninstalled the game and installed again, same for EA APP... didn't work. Looked for a fix on forums and YouTube and it looks like I'm not the only one who has this problem. Funny that a singelplayer game needs internet connection and the EA APP to run on PC.

I would recommend buying the game for console.
Dragon Age Inquisition is one of my favorite game.
And (EA APP) is now one of my nightmares...
Game won't launch, it wants me to install an app from Microsoft to launch it? No clue.

EA took it of steam or smthn and now my copy doesn't work

fuck EA fuck steam for doing nothing, and fuck capitalism whilst i'm at it

Great game but broken on Steam. Launch issues have plagued this game for years but seem to have been resolved on Origin. On Steam, you may or may not be able to get it to launch ... and possibly end up like me - lots of stuffing around, get it to run once or twice and then back to nothing. Get it on Origin if you want to play it. (There's loads of troubleshooting advice out there, and just as many frustrated people saying it doesn't work. Caveat emptor.)

I owned this forever on Origins, but now with EA Play you can't buy the dlc, you have to get the EA Play pass. This version they sell on steam includes all the dlc, plus it goes on sale regularly here for the cost of two months of EA Play pass.

TLDR; amazing game, get it on here not ea play

This game is every bit as amazing as Origins and II in my opinion. Combat is fun, and the story is top-notch. Maybe the worlds are a bit on the big-and-spread-out side, but that doesn't take away from the experience. This is an underrated game.

So....the shards, the bottles of thedas, the mosaics, the astrariums, among others - make this game quite a pain in the behind. On the other hand, the character's interactions were nicely done (Ej. Varrik & Cassandra or a romance with Josy) - the ending was also pretty sweet. It's just such a shame that the fetch quests take 70% of the bulk of the game and leave the user fighting with tooth and nails to be able to enjoy these very few enjoyable moments. If you're waiting for the next release I'd suggest you play through to understand what's going on, without committing too much time into it.

I have over 100 hours of this on xbox. The game has very engaging and challenging combat with tons of variety. There is a lot of things to do in this game and a lot variation in the combat and gameplay.

Narratively, mechanically, and gameplay-wise, Inquisition is the most polished and well-done of the DA trilogy. Most of the negative reviews you'll see for this game here are from requiring the EA launcher (which is fair, because the EA launcher is ass).

Great companions, Varric, Cassandra, Dorian, they are one of the best Bioware ever made. Pretty good combat system and skill system, good main and companion quests, big amount of banter between companions and dialogues with companions, creating your own world state is another good thing, not all choices are significant from previous game, but it is to be expected. Battle with dragons are epic. Great DLC-s, Trespasser is the best thing Dragon Age ever had. Visually game looks great even in 2021. The only downside is side quests, they are repetitive and generally not interesting, except the few ones. GOTY was well deserved back then and I hope DA4 will be better

PS. 2024
It is not
Really fun! With an engaging story, pretty graphics, great character customization and excellent romance routes, there's nothing more to ask for!

Played the hell out of this on my playstation, and bought it on here. After playing (and enjoying thought not as much) Veilguard I decided to come back and play through it again. It's definitely worth it. Especially since I never got to play through the DLC on my other system.

Battles are fun.
Hate running around.
Mod-friendly, sort of.
Worth of multiple playthroughs.
And why do so many like creating an ugly inquisitor?

There's one simple reason I can't recommend Inquisition. the weird MMO comabt sytem is just terrible and teh game REALLY makes you use it. From wandering around open worlds that are mostly empty and lifeless to encouraging you to fight a insane amount of dragon bosses that are almost all optional. Now that said I have finished the game 3 times and that's because its writing is nearly as good as the first games. Almost all the party members are outstanding, the main villian and the main plot are really good. I dont particuallarly care of the games look, but at time it does look really good, usually when the main villian is on screen he just commands so much attention.

Unlike the previous two Dragon Age games, the main character is a non-person, and it almost feels as if the game resents the fact that the player is there at all. They would have much rather picked one of their NPCs to be the Green Hand Dude and done away with the player altogether.

The story is "there are evil portals" and the game consists of standing in a room with some demons until you close the portals. That's what you do about 15 minutes in, and the rest of the game appears to be a big Green Portal Closing simulator.

For some baffling reason they did the Mass Effect Andromeda-style open world. At the 3 hour mark, I opened my map to see literally twenty four quest markers crammed into a completely superfluous generic "forest" map and decided to uninstall the game. I'm not here to waste time hunting 10 Snow Oxen to get 10 Snow Oxen Appendices. Utterly absurd they went this direction for the game.

Game was good in it's day, had plenty to do and a fairly engaging story. Classes felt fleshed out and improved from prior entries. Magic felt INCREDIBLE. Two handed weapons felt amazing, loved my dwarf two handed warrior!

However now with the EA Play Application the game is a mess (If you can even get it to run in the first place).

I hear some people have luck with the support team at EA but I did not.

Try GOG for the 1st game, but it doesn't have the other 2 so who knows when we will have playable version again.

If you somehow manage to get it to run, have a wonderful time with a enjoyable game.

The story is absolutely amazing. I wish i would have tried this game awhile back. This is definitely a favorite of mine now. The combat is really good and smooth. There are so many characters you can interact with and the decisions you make do make a difference in how your story plays out. By the way the main menu music is probably the best I have ever heard. The mod support for this game is incredible and theres enough mods on nexus mods to suit everyones playstyle. I would definitely give this game a try especially if its on sale. I got it in a bundle with mass effect andromeda for just under $10 and I loved both of them. It was the game of the year edition for dragon age inquisition so it comes with all the dlc as well which is fantastic. I have only done one playthrough at the time of this review and completed all the dlc and the main story. This was a fantastic game.

If you liked playing the older Dragon Age games, or are looking for that flavor but with a more modern approach, then check out this game. The open world zones are filled with interesting things to do and find, and the story has many twists and turns fun for returning and new players alike. Maybe not the peak of gaming but one you can easily sink 60+ hours in and still be having a great time.

Despite all the many flaws and bugs, the game still holds its place as one of the best in the Dragon Age series. There is much to explore and collect making it a great pass-by game. The DLC adds a lot of extra hours to the table and if you really spend the time to get that sweet 100% completion, it is very much worth it.
one of the best rpg games available to play even thought it came out in 2014. you dont really need to play the dragon age series to play it and have fun either.

Man, this game is fantastic. I can see why this game won over 130 awards.

I only have managed to get through the prologue so far, but I can already tell this game will have significant replay value, not even just because of the different races, but the different dialogue options as well.

This game is definitely one you can find yourself getting lost in, and I look forward to continuing the story on this one as I continue playing through it.

Don't play this game in 2021, it's not worth even 10$. Game have infinity load screen and a bunch of boring side quest. The main quest make you fetch some super hidden items which you have to run in circles to find them and then you don't and have to youtube your way through quest because this game forces you to grind your way through exploring every inch of corners to find a dumb quest item to proceed. Do yourself a favor and dont even play this in 2021.

A well made narrative rpg with many choice and consequences. The biggest highlight of the game was the characters and lore of the world. A major gripe was the constant fetch quests and the open world is too big for the type of rpg dragon age is. also the DRM sucks.

Great as all Dragon Age games. Loved playing this game. Tons of lore and tons of fun. If I had to pick something to improve it would be combat. Aside from that it's a great game. Everyone should at least try it!

TROUBLESHOOTING THE GAME, THE GAME.
ENJOY HOURS OF CONTENT IN THE FORUM PAGES BEFORE THE GAME EVEN STARTS. (because it literally wont start)
Groundbreaking stuff EA thank you for this seamless software experience.

Just started getting into this genre of games and man this was really good. The last fight just felt epic. Exactly how it should of felt. Haven't played the DLC but definitely going to give them a try after a break XD
very fun cast of characters. Reminds of me a mix of Balders Gate 3 and World of Warcraft in the best way possible.

I only play this game because DA:O is unplayable on PC due to it constantly crashing or running at 3 FPS and it's the closest thing I can get to it. Is it great? No, not really. Is it fun? Sort of. Is it a disgrace compared to the original? Absolutely. But alas, albeit barely, its Dragon Age.

I like the story and for the most part it has some great Dragon Age lore and world building. My only problem is that the open world side quests are SUPER boring and kinda tedious. The game is a product from a time when every developer was like throwing open world into everything.

If I were to describe this game in one word it would be 'boring'.
If I were to put it more fully, it would be that this game is trying to be another step for DA's evolution that falls backwards painfully on it's ass.
From janky controls, to trying to be hyper-realistic, horrible color grading, bloated open-world and quests, and even less than interesting to unwanted members of the cast; this game leaves much to be wanted.
On top of this, most of the main storyline and ending revolves around a man who I could barely grow to give any attention or care to, when every word that came out of his mouth was how start he was and how he hates modern elves, while constantly lying to your face.
For a series that thrives on it's companions, only Varric and Dorian are the ones that I can stand, which is rather sad.

I enjoy exploring open-world games and searching for new things. I loved the lore and historical references that led me back to the previous Dragon Age games. It's replay-ability and varying character selections and dialogue options change the way your characters influence the gameplay. Dragon Age hooked me in with the first game, the lore was engaging and made you want to know more about Thedas!

I want to say this game is an alright play. IF I could ever finish it. It randomly uninstalled my game and now I cannot reinstall it without my save files intact. I have tried numerous fixes and none of them work. A collective FUCK YOU to EA and BioWare for not fixing this issue on a ten year old game.

Never thought I would welcome this title with open arms after the deception I got from the plot / story of Dragon Age 2. I mean, don't get me wrong but the twist in this story gave me hope that the devs knew their mistakes about the second title, also the semi open world is a great addition. I am crossing fingers for the next D.A !

No game has ever left me quite so invested as this one. The gameplay, and the story really got me hooked. First introduction to the Dragon Age series and looking forward to immersing myself to the rest of the game

I like Dragon Age, It does not like me back. I had to start DAO at least thrice because the first time I created a Ranger, bad choice, the game does not tell you, but playing as anything but a Male Human Mage is pretty much playing an NPC because the story on ALL of them focuses on Mages and how Humans pretty much just bully everyone else. For DA2, I went for a Female Human Mage, still had to start the game again once, I don't quite remember why, still, I like the story even if Mage centric, I did enjoy 2.

Now, about this one, DA3: I like seeing familiar faces, not all of them the ones I WANT to see so far, but 40 hours in, with just a couple of missions to finish in the Hinderlands or whatever, turns out that the game thinks my Hawke is Male, so I do some research and turns out none of my previous decisions from the first 2 games were recorded, turns out you need to go to their webpage and MANUALLY fill your decisions for the game to know about them, and you cannot change them 40 hours in and expect the game to update, so, yes, starting all over again. Thanks to AI at least I got to retrieve my character appearance customization and it kind of feels like I am playing the same game... If I had to start from a very old save.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (76%): players love the story and characters.
Many complain about combat, bugs and crashes.

details.text: Players with under 2 hours are far less positive, at 26%, than players with over 50 hours, at 88%.
Buyers should also know that accounts and launcher trouble is a smaller but real complaint, with one reviewer saying "Can't recommend until they fix all the issues" with the EA app.
